sents.t: I have worked at Oakville Books for exactly one year, and on Monday I started my new job as assistant manager.
Mr. Lee has moved to the new Riverside store, so now I’m in charge here four days a week.
On Tuesday morning, I held my first team meeting.
I had never led a meeting before, so I was nervous.
The night before, I prepared an agenda and printed five copies.
There are four people on my team.
Tina has worked here for six years, and she knows every book in the store.
Jake started in March.
He’s a college student, and he loves comics.
Maria and Ben joined last month.
“Thank you for coming,” I began.
“First, I want to hear your ideas.”
At first, nobody said anything.
Then Tina raised her hand.
“We’ve had the same window display since April. Customers have stopped looking at it.”
Jake suggested a monthly comic night for teenagers, and Maria offered to start a book club in Spanish.
By the end of the meeting, we had a list of eight ideas and a deadline for each one.
Later, I called Mr. Lee.
“How did it go?” he asked.
“Better than I expected,” I said.
“I think I’ve found my team.”
